Binomial Theorem and its Simple Applications

scope_interpretation.basis: NTA JEE Main 2026 Paper 1 Mathematics syllabus, strict reading (user decision 2026-10-07: strict syllabus only).
unit_2_included: ordered pairs, a + ib, powers of i, conjugate, algebra, square roots
Argand plane, modulus, principal argument in (-pi, pi], polar form, simple loci and regions, extremal modulus
quadratics with real and complex coefficients, discriminant and nature of roots, sign, range and extrema of quadratic expressions, location of roots, equations reducible to quadratics
relations between roots and coefficients, symmetric functions, transformed-root equations, common roots, S_n recurrences from the quadratic itself
omega only as a root of x^2 + x + 1 = 0 (5 items, including two with roots 2 omega type)

rotation theorem and argument of (z3 - z1)/(z2 - z1)
cubic and higher polynomial theory except equations reducible to quadratics

special series beyond AP, GP and AM-GM
trigonometric equations and heights and distances

unit_scope_briefs.U01:
# Unit 1: Sets, Relations and Functions

Official 2026 text: "Sets and their representation; Union, intersection and complement of sets and their algebraic properties; Power set; Relations, type of relations, equivalence relations, functions; one-one, into and onto functions, the composition of functions."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Roster/set-builder forms, subsets, power set and its size, union/intersection/complement/difference, De Morgan and other algebraic laws, Venn-diagram counting n(A union B) and three-set counting
- Cartesian product, relations as subsets, domain and range of a relation, number of relations, reflexive/symmetric/transitive/equivalence relations, equivalence classes, counting relations with given properties on small sets
- Functions as relations, domain/range for simple functions, one-one, many-one, into, onto, bijective, counting functions/injections/surjections between finite sets, composition f o g and its domain, invertibility of a bijection

Out of scope (do not write):
- Inverse trigonometric functions (Unit 14)
- limits/continuity (Unit 7)
- binary operations
- detailed graphs of functions (Unit 7)
unit_scope_briefs.U02:
# Unit 2: Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations (all Class XI)

Official 2026 text: "Complex numbers as ordered pairs of reals, Representation of complex numbers
in the form a + ib and their representation in a plane, Argand diagram, algebra of complex numbers,
modulus and argument (or amplitude) of a complex number, Quadratic equations in real and complex
number systems and their solutions; Relations between roots and coefficients, nature of roots, the
formation of quadratic equations with given roots."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Ordered-pair definition, equality, a + ib, powers of i, conjugate and its properties, sum,
  product, quotient, multiplicative inverse, square roots of a complex number.
- Argand plane, modulus, argument and principal argument (always state $(-\pi, \pi]$), polar
  form $r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)$, modulus/argument of products and quotients, triangle
  inequality, simple loci: $|z - z_1| = r$, $|z - z_1| = |z - z_2|$, $\operatorname{Re}$/$\operatorname{Im}$
  conditions, regions, distance between points, geometric meaning of $|z_1 - z_2|$.
- Quadratics with real or complex coefficients, solving in R and C, discriminant and nature of
  roots, conjugate-pair property for real coefficients, sum/product of roots, symmetric functions,
  transformed-root equations, formation from given roots, common root conditions, sign and range
  of a quadratic expression, max/min of a quadratic, conditions on location of roots (both
  positive, opposite signs, both greater than k, k between the roots), equations reducible to
  quadratics (in $x^2$, $|x|$, $a^x$, $x + \frac{1}{x}$), integral-root and parameter questions,
  recurrences $S_n = \alpha^n + \beta^n$ obtained from the quadratic itself.
- $\omega$ only as a root of $x^2 + x + 1 = 0$ (so $\omega^3 = 1$ follows); at most 4 items total.

Out of scope (do not write): De Moivre's theorem, nth roots of unity beyond the quadratic case,
rotation theorem / $\frac{z_3 - z_1}{z_2 - z_1}$ angle arguments, Euler $e^{i\theta}$ calculus,
cubic or higher polynomial theory (except reducible-to-quadratic), mathematical induction.
unit_scope_briefs.U03:
# Unit 3: Matrices and Determinants

Official 2026 text: "Matrices, algebra of matrices, type of matrices, determinants and matrices of order two and three, evaluation of determinants, area of triangles using determinants; Adjoint and inverse of a square matrix; Test of consistency and solution of simultaneous linear equations in two or three variables using matrices."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Order, types (diagonal, scalar, identity, triangular, symmetric, skew-symmetric, orthogonal via A A^T = I, idempotent, nilpotent, involutory), transpose, algebra, powers of matrices, trace, commuting matrices
- Determinants of order 2 and 3, properties, evaluation by properties, |kA|, |AB|, |A^T|, determinant equations, area of a triangle and collinearity
- Minors, cofactors, adjoint, inverse, |adj A| = |A|^(n-1), adj(adj A), (AB)^-1, inverse via A^2 relations (Cayley-Hamilton style identities for 2x2 given as stated facts only)
- Systems in 2 or 3 variables: consistency, unique/infinitely many/no solution, parameter values, homogeneous systems and non-trivial solutions, matrix method

Out of scope (do not write):
- Rank of a matrix by name
- eigenvalues by name
- Cramer's rule is allowed only as a method; no 4x4 determinants
unit_scope_briefs.U04:
# Unit 4: Permutations and Combinations

Official 2026 text: "The fundamental principle of counting, permutations and combinations; Meaning of P(n, r) and C(n, r). Simple applications."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Fundamental principle of counting, permutations with and without repetition, arrangements with identical objects, restrictions (together/never together/fixed positions), digit and word formation, rank of a word in dictionary order
- Combinations, properties of C(n, r), selections with restrictions, committees, at least/at most, geometric counting (lines, triangles, diagonals), number of divisors, distribution into groups of given sizes, simple identical-object distributions via selection

Out of scope (do not write):
- Circular permutations beyond a one-line note (avoid)
- derangement formula
- multinomial/generating functions
- inclusion-exclusion beyond three sets
- probability (Unit 13)
unit_scope_briefs.U05:
# Unit 5: Binomial Theorem and its Simple Applications

Official 2026 text: "Binomial theorem for a positive integral index, general term and middle term and simple applications."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Expansion for positive integer index, general term, specific coefficients, term independent of x, middle term(s), number of terms, coefficients in products like (1 + x)^m (1 - x)^n
- Sum of binomial coefficients and simple coefficient identities, numerically greatest term only in simple cases, remainder and divisibility applications, last digits, approximations, comparison of large numbers, rational terms in expansions involving surds

Out of scope (do not write):
- Binomial theorem for negative or fractional index
- multinomial theorem
- summations requiring calculus beyond basic
unit_scope_briefs.U06:
# Unit 6: Sequence and Series

Official 2026 text: "Arithmetic and Geometric progressions, insertion of arithmetic, geometric means between two given numbers, Relation between A.M and G.M."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- AP: nth term, sum of n terms, properties, conditions for terms in AP, problems with S_n given as a function of n
- GP: nth term, sum of n terms, sum to infinity for |r| < 1, properties, recurring decimals as GP
- Insertion of arithmetic and geometric means, relation between AM and GM, AM-GM inequality for minimum/maximum problems, mixed AP-GP problems

Out of scope (do not write):
- Harmonic progression as a separate topic
- arithmetico-geometric series
- sums of n^2, n^3 and method of differences
- Sigma of special series
unit_scope_briefs.U07:
# Unit 7: Limit, Continuity and Differentiability

Official 2026 text: "Real-valued functions, algebra of functions; polynomial, rational, trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions; inverse functions. Graphs of simple functions. Limits, continuity and differentiability. Differentiation of the sum, difference, product and quotient of two functions. Differentiation of trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, logarithmic, exponential, composite and implicit functions; derivatives of order upto two, Applications of derivatives: Rate of change of quantities, monotonic-Increasing and decreasing functions, Maxima and minima of functions of one variable."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Real functions: domain, range, algebra of functions, even/odd, periodicity of simple functions, inverse of a function, graphs of simple functions (modulus, greatest integer, signum, exponential, log)
- Limits: algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic standard limits, 1^infinity form, left and right limits, limits at infinity
- Continuity and differentiability at a point and on intervals, piecewise functions, greatest integer and modulus functions, parameter values for continuity/differentiability
- Differentiation rules, chain rule, implicit, inverse trigonometric, logarithmic differentiation, second derivatives
- Applications: rate of change, increasing/decreasing, local and absolute maxima/minima of one-variable functions

Out of scope (do not write):
- Parametric differentiation (not listed)
- L'Hospital's rule may be used in solutions but not named as required
- tangents and normals (not listed)
- Rolle's and mean value theorems (not listed)
- approximations by differentials
unit_scope_briefs.U08:
# Unit 8: Integral Calculus

Official 2026 text: "Integral as an anti-derivative, Fundamental integrals involving algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions. Integration by substitution, by parts and by partial fractions. Integration using trigonometric identities. Evaluation of simple integrals of the type dx/(x^2 +/- a^2), dx/sqrt(x^2 +/- a^2), dx/(a^2 - x^2), dx/sqrt(a^2 - x^2), dx/(ax^2 + bx + c), dx/sqrt(ax^2 + bx + c), (px + q)/(ax^2 + bx + c) dx, (px + q)/sqrt(ax^2 + bx + c) dx, sqrt(a^2 +/- x^2) dx, sqrt(x^2 - a^2) dx. The fundamental theorem of calculus, properties of definite integrals. Evaluation of definite integrals, determining areas of the regions bounded by simple curves in standard forms."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Indefinite integrals: fundamental integrals, substitution, trigonometric identities, by parts, e^x(f + f') form, partial fractions, the listed special forms
- Definite integrals: fundamental theorem, properties (King's property, even/odd, periodicity, splitting at points of non-smoothness), greatest integer and modulus integrands, derivative of an integral with variable limits
- Areas bounded by simple curves: lines, parabolas, circles, ellipses, modulus curves, between two curves

Out of scope (do not write):
- Reduction formulae
- definite integral as a limit of a sum (avoid)
- Walli's formula by name
- double integrals
unit_scope_briefs.U09:
# Unit 9: Differential Equations

Official 2026 text: "Ordinary differential equations, their order and degree, the solution of differential equation by the method of separation of variables, solution of a homogeneous and linear differential equation."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Order and degree (including when degree is undefined)
- variables separable, including substitutions reducing to separable
- homogeneous equations
- linear first-order equations, integrating factor
- simple applications (growth/decay, curves with given slope property) solved by these methods

Out of scope (do not write):
- Formation of differential equations by eliminating constants (not listed)
- Bernoulli equations
- exact equations
- second-order equations
unit_scope_briefs.U10:
# Unit 10: Co-ordinate Geometry

Official 2026 text: "Cartesian system of rectangular coordinates in a plane, distance formula, sections formula, locus and its equation, the slope of a line, parallel and perpendicular lines, intercepts of a line on the co-ordinate axis. Straight line: Various forms of equations of a line, intersection of lines, angles between two lines, conditions for concurrence of three lines, the distance of a point from a line, co-ordinate of the centroid, orthocentre and circumcentre of a triangle. Circle, conic sections: A standard form of equations of a circle, the general form of the equation of a circle, its radius and centre, equation of a circle when the endpoints of a diameter are given, points of intersection of a line and a circle with the centre at the origin and sections of conics, equations of conic sections (parabola, ellipse and hyperbola) in standard forms."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Distance, section formula, locus, slope, parallel/perpendicular, intercepts, centroid/orthocentre/circumcentre/incentre of a triangle, area of triangle by coordinates
- Lines: all standard forms, intersection, angle between lines, concurrency, distance of a point from a line, distance between parallel lines, foot of perpendicular and image of a point in a line, family of lines through an intersection
- Circles: standard and general forms, centre and radius, diameter form, circle through three points, intersection of a line with a circle centred at the origin (including the tangency condition c^2 = a^2(1 + m^2) derived from intersection), position of a point
- Parabola, ellipse, hyperbola in standard forms: focus, directrix, vertex, axes, eccentricity, latus rectum, focal distances, identifying a conic from its equation, finding equation from given data, intersection of a line with a conic as a quadratic

Out of scope (do not write):
- Tangents and normals to conics as a separate theory (not listed)
- chord of contact, pole/polar
- family of circles and radical axis
- parametric forms beyond simple use
- pair of straight lines
- rotation of axes
unit_scope_briefs.U11:
# Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry

Official 2026 text: "Coordinates of a point in space, the distance between two points, section formula, direction ratios and direction cosines and the angle between two intersecting lines. Equation of a line; Skew lines, the shortest distance between them and its equation."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Coordinates, distance, section formula, centroid in space, direction ratios and cosines (l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1), angle between two lines
- Equation of a line in vector and Cartesian forms, point on a line, foot of perpendicular from a point to a line, image of a point in a line, intersection of two lines, collinearity
- Skew lines, shortest distance between two lines (skew and parallel), condition for coplanarity/intersection of two lines, equation of the line of shortest distance (only in simple cases)

Out of scope (do not write):
- Planes (not in the 2026 syllabus): no plane equations, angle between line and plane, distance from a plane
- spheres
unit_scope_briefs.U12:
# Unit 12: Vector Algebra

Official 2026 text: "Vectors and scalars, the addition of vectors, components of a vector in two dimensions and three-dimensional spaces, scalar and vector products."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Vectors and scalars, addition, components, position vectors, section formula, unit vectors, collinearity, linear combinations
- Scalar product: angle, projection, perpendicularity, |a + b| and |a - b| relations, work-type applications
- Vector product: area of parallelogram and triangle, unit vector perpendicular to two vectors, |a x b|^2 + (a.b)^2 = |a|^2|b|^2, solving simple vector equations using cross product

Out of scope (do not write):
- Scalar triple product and vector triple product (not listed)
- coplanarity via triple products
- reciprocal systems
unit_scope_briefs.U13:
# Unit 13: Statistics and Probability

Official 2026 text: "Measures of dispersion; calculation of mean, median, mode of grouped and ungrouped data, calculation of standard deviation, variance and mean deviation for grouped and ungrouped data. Probability: Probability of an event, addition and multiplication theorems of probability, Baye's theorem, probability distribution of a random variable."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Mean, median, mode of grouped and ungrouped data, mean deviation about mean/median, variance and standard deviation, effect of change of origin and scale, combined mean and variance, corrected values after a wrong observation
- Probability of events, addition theorem, multiplication theorem, conditional probability, independent events
- Total probability and Bayes' theorem, probability distribution of a discrete random variable, its mean and variance

Out of scope (do not write):
- Binomial distribution by name (the 2026 syllabus does not list it); Bernoulli trials only as a plain probability calculation
- correlation and regression
- continuous distributions
- coefficient of variation is allowed as a ratio only
unit_scope_briefs.U14:
# Unit 14: Trigonometry

Official 2026 text: "Trigonometrical identities and trigonometrical functions, inverse trigonometrical functions their properties."

In scope (interpretation used for this bank):
- Trigonometric ratios of allied and compound angles, multiple and sub-multiple angles, sum-to-product and product-to-sum, conditional identities (A + B + C = pi), values of special angles like 15, 18, 36 degrees
- Trigonometric functions: domain, range, period, signs, maximum and minimum of expressions like a sin x + b cos x and quadratic expressions in sin x, products of cosines in GP
- Inverse trigonometric functions: principal values, domains and ranges, properties, sum/difference formulas, simplification, equations in inverse trigonometric functions

Out of scope (do not write):
- Trigonometric equations and general solutions (not listed)
- heights and distances
- properties of triangles (sine/cosine rule, not listed)
